title: agent-tracer MCP server manifest (MCP/<name>/mcp.json)
description: Declares how the agent-tracer runner discovers and launches an MCP server placed under the MCP/ directory. One subdirectory = one server. Servers are auto-registered by default (default all); YAML config may narrow the set via mcp.include / mcp.exclude.

$schema.description: This schema, so an editor can complete and check the manifest as it is written. Every packaged manifest opens with "../mcp.schema.json"; declared here because additionalProperties is false and a manifest that names its schema must still validate against it.

manifest_version.description: Manifest schema version. Bump only with a coordinated runner change.

name.description: Server name. MUST equal the directory name (MCP/<name>/). Used in YAML include/exclude and as the tool namespace prefix (mcp:<name>/<tool>).

description.description: One-line summary of what the server provides. Recorded in trajectory metadata.

version.description: Server implementation version (semver recommended). Recorded in trajectory metadata for reproducibility.

transport.description: How the runner connects. stdio: runner spawns `command` and speaks MCP over stdin/stdout. http: runner connects to a streamable-HTTP endpoint at `url` (server lifecycle is external).

command.description: Executable to spawn (stdio only). Required when transport is stdio. Resolved on PATH; use "uv" for uv-run based servers.

args.description: Arguments for command (stdio only). Relative paths are resolved against this manifest's directory.

url.description: MCP endpoint URL (http only). Required when transport is http.

env.description: Environment variables passed to the spawned process. A value of the form "env:VAR_NAME" (e.g. "env:SEARCH_API_KEY") is resolved from the runner's .env/environment at startup, and an unresolvable one aborts the run (fail-fast, consistent with api_key/reasoning_key). Any other value is passed on exactly as written — correct for a setting, never for a secret: a key written here is a key published with the repository.

headers.description: HTTP headers sent with every request (http only). Same rule as env: "env:VAR_NAME" (e.g. "env:CONTEXT7_API_KEY") is resolved at startup and an unresolvable one aborts the run; anything else is sent exactly as written — correct for Accept, never for a key. Omit the property entirely on a stdio server; declaring it, even empty, is refused.

sandbox_options.description: This server attaches to the task's sandbox and needs environment.options to do it (stdio only). Those options are where a backend's credentials go, so AGENT_TRACER_OPTIONS is sent only to servers that declare this. The rest of the sandbox description (AGENT_TRACER_ENV_TYPE, _SANDBOX_ID, _WORKDIR, _HOST_DIR, _USER) goes to every server.

startup_timeout_s.description: Max seconds to wait for the server to complete the MCP initialize handshake. The client connects every selected server in one sequential pass, so what is enforced is the sum of the selected manifests' values; exceeding it aborts the attempt rather than waiting for the runner's task timeout. A server's first `uv run` builds its environment and can exceed this on a cold cache.

call_timeout_s.description: Per-tool-call timeout in seconds, enforced on both transports. A call that exceeds it is cancelled and comes back to the model as a timeout result, so the agent loop continues rather than losing the trajectory.

tools.description: Optional declared tool list, for documentation and contract tests. The authoritative list always comes from MCP tool discovery at runtime; contract tests warn when the two diverge.
